rows.text: On 24 November 2025, a Microsoft cost incident happened because the price per unit went up for the platform and web teams. This mattered because it added $171.01 in extra cost so far to resources like law-acme-prod. The incident ended on 6 December 2025, and the next step is to review the updated pricing.

Usage went up for resource aks-prod-nodepool1 starting on 15 December 2025, which caused the daily cost to jump from $34.78 to $54.43 and added $356.57 in extra expenses. This incident has ended on 31 December 2025. Please review the platform team's Virtual Machines usage on Microsoft to confirm operations are back to normal.

New spend on Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud and Amazon Simple Storage Service started on 2 January 2026 because of a project tag customs change by the web team, causing an extra cost so far of $3,574.85. This will continue to add an extra cost per month if not fixed of $420.92, jumping the daily cost when detected to $12.44 from a usual daily cost of $0.00. Please have the web team review and stop these unauthorized AWS resources immediately.

On 28 February 2026, the ml team started a new Microsoft Virtual Machines resource named vm-ml-loadtest-25 that added $387.07 in extra cost so far. This cost matters because the usual daily cost was $0.00 and jumped to $12.10 daily before the incident ended on 31 March 2026. The next step is to review this spend with the ml team to prevent similar charges on future tests.

New Microsoft spending started in region westeurope on 11 April 2026 and ended on 4 June 2026, driven by services like Virtual Machines, Bandwidth, and Storage. This caused an extra cost so far of $1,463.85 compared to a usual daily cost of $0.00. The platform team should review the daily cost of $27.17 from 11 April 2026 to ensure this new spend does not return.

Virtual Machines, Bandwidth, and Storage resources for the platform team on Microsoft spent more than usual because spend rose above its usual level, starting on 16 April 2026 and ending on 4 June 2026. This caused an extra cost so far of $1,056.79, moving the daily cost from $0.00 to $22.83 by the time it was detected on 30 April 2026. Review these items to prevent future unexpected Microsoft charges.

A commitment discount ended on 10 May 2026 for vm-sql-prod-01 and vm-sql-prod-02, causing daily costs to jump from $28.55 to $48.38 and adding $2,856.39 in extra costs so far. If we do nothing, we will waste an extra $603.76 per month. The next step is to renew the commitment discount for the data team to stop these higher charges.

Usage went up for resource law-acme-prod on Microsoft Log Analytics starting on 5 July 2026, which ran until it ended on 15 July 2026. This incident increased your spending by an extra cost so far of $1,841.46 because the daily cost jumped from $15.26 to $174.32 when detected. Have the platform team review the usage changes for this resource to prevent future spikes.

On 16 July 2026, untagged AWS resources caused extra spending that totaled $3,320.41 by the time the issue ended on 17 September 2026. Daily costs jumped from $1.66 to $10.37 because seven new items appeared on Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud. Please apply the correct team tag to these resources to prevent future billing surprises.

An AWS cost incident happened on 29 July 2026 for the web team because usage went up on Amazon Simple Storage Service. This caused extra spending so far of $348.76 while the daily cost rose to $137.57. The incident ended on 31 July 2026, and we should review the usage for resource tw-media-exports.

Costs spiked on 25 July 2026 because cloud usage went up while resources were untagged, driving total extra spending to $3,335.61. This money matters because it significantly exceeds our usual daily cost of $2.31, reaching $66.65 when detected. Please apply the ml team tag to the affected Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud, Virtual Machines, and Storage services.

A new resource named loadtest-ml-tmp or exp-12 appeared in AWS on 8 August 2026 and is still running, which added extra_cost_so_far of $544.02. If left unfixed, this will add extra_cost_per_month_if_not_fixed of $165.90 to our cloud bill. Please review and stop this untagged ml service immediately.

AWS costs for Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud rose because usage went up starting on 2 August 2026, causing an extra cost so far of $2,121.70. This matters because daily spending increased from $86.84 to $142.47 by the time it was detected on 16 August 2026. The next step is to review the untagged, data, ml, platform, and web teams since the incident ended on 17 September 2026.

A cost incident started on 20 August 2026 because usage went up for resources loadtest-ml-tmp, exp-12, and law-acme-prod. This unexpected usage increased the extra cost so far to $269.69, while the daily cost rose from $23.68 to $34.43 when detected. Although the status ended on 21 September 2026, the next step is to review the untagged, ml, and platform teams.

Usage went up for resource stwebassetsprod on 25 August 2026, causing extra costs of $626.46 for the web team. The daily cost jumped from $10.12 to $175.16 before the incident ended on 28 August 2026. Please review the Bandwidth and Storage services to confirm the issue is fully resolved.

On 29 August 2026, increased usage on Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud caused the daily cost to jump from $3.02 to $10.63, adding $251.14 in extra expenses so far. If the data and ml teams do not fix these resources, it will cost an extra $262.32 per month. Please check the batch-1 and loadtest-ml-tmp resources to shut them down if they are no longer needed.

Usage went up on the AWS platform service Amazon CloudWatch for resource /acme/prod/app starting on 31 August 2026, which added an extra cost so far of $532.13. The daily cost jumped from the usual_daily_cost of $6.06 to $46.06 when detected, and the incident ended on 12 September 2026. Review the platform usage for Amazon CloudWatch to prevent future cost spikes.

The data team should move the tw-data-lake resource from the Standard tier to the Standard-IA tier. This change will save $410.13 a month and $4,921.56 a year because it is rarely read. The next step is to set up a lifecycle rule to make the move happen.

Review the updated unit pricing on these resources to ensure your budget accounts for the higher rates going forward.
